title: Glessner's granite joints now read as shadowed recesses
items: On the Glessner House's rock-faced granite, the sky light now falls off into every mortar joint, along each stone's pitched edge and into the window reveals, so a wall in shade reads stone by stone instead of as flat bands with bright seams.
The shading is computed from the house's own modelled stones and touches only the sky's light; the sunlit faces are unchanged.
On desktop. Phones keep the lighter model and its finer stone texture for now.
